record.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen with broad availability and agentic-workflow claims
record.summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Hydrogen on 12 November 2026 and says it is rolling out across Gemini API, AI Studio, business products, the Gemini app and Search. Google positions it as a faster execution model for everyday coding and agentic workflows, offers a 1-million-token context window, and lists API prices of $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens. Google reports an Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score of 51 at its default high thinking level (54 at xhigh), Terminal-Bench 4.1 score of 57% versus 18.2% for Gemini 3.8 Flash, and an Antigravity Orchestrator result near Gemini 4 Carbon task success while using 24% less quota and finishing 19% faster on Terminal-Bench 4.0. These are provider-reported figures, not independently reproduced in this review.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Google announced Gemini 4 Hydrogen on 12 November 2026 and says it is rolling out across consumer, developer and enterprise surfaces.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Google lists a 1-million-token context window and API prices of $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Google reports Hydrogen scores 51 at high and 54 at xhigh on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, scores 57% on Terminal-Bench 4.1 versus Gemini 3.8 Flash at 18.2%, and in Antigravity Orchestrator achieves near-Carbon Terminal-Bench 4.0 success while using 24% less quota and finishing 19% faster.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Google’s model card says Hydrogen did not show a material general-capability increase over Gemini 4 Argon under its assessment, while targeted cyber and biological capability tests reached alert thresholds but not the corresponding critical capability levels; the full Safety & Security Report was still forthcoming.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: Independent reproduction of the reported performance, safety and efficiency results, and realized cost savings in external workloads, were not established in this review.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent matched evaluation of Hydrogen’s reported benchmark performance, tool-use reliability or relative latency was inspected.
The claimed 24% quota reduction and 19% faster Orchestrator result have no inspected task-level methodology or external replication.
The model card says the full Gemini 4 Hydrogen Safety & Security Report is forthcoming; it is needed to inspect detailed methods behind alert-threshold and safety claims.

brief.importance_rationale: If the broad availability and reported execution efficiency hold across relevant workloads, model routing between deep-reasoning and execution models could change engineering throughput and inference economics for many teams. The score reflects that possible consequence, not confidence in Google’s measurements.
limitations: All reported benchmark scores and workflow efficiency figures in the launch are provider claims; no independent matched reproduction was inspected.
Artificial Analysis Index, Terminal-Bench 4.0 and 4.1 scores are different measurements and cannot be directly combined.
The API prices are posted rates, not measured cost per successful task; output length, thinking level and workflow routing can change realized cost.

The model card reports a March 2026 knowledge cutoff and a 5.57 percentage-point increase in unjustified refusals versus Gemini 3.8 Flash; the full Safety & Security Report was forthcoming at review time.

relationships.summary: Both concern Google’s November 2026 Gemini 4 model-series rollout; Carbon was opened to broader access the prior day, while Hydrogen is presented as the faster execution model.

brief.summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Hydrogen on 12 November 2026 and says it is rolling out across Gemini API, AI Studio, business products, the Gemini app and Search. technical.claimed_result: Google reports benchmark scores, relative speed, reduced quota use and internal safety-evaluation results; these are not independently reproduced here.
technical.compute_or_cost: Posted API price is $1.50/M input and $7.50/M output tokens. Realized cost per successful task and independent latency/quota measurements are unknown.
technical.demonstrated_result: The dated official release and model card establish Google’s announcement, stated rollout, posted API prices and provider-published evaluations.
technical.implementation_status: Google says rollout begins globally on 2026-11-12 across listed surfaces.
technical.mechanism: Google describes Hydrogen as adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon and optimized for rapid execution; its Antigravity Orchestrator dynamically switches between models for complex workflows.
technical.regime: Provider-reported benchmark and product rollout; Hydrogen is adapted from Carbon; default high versus xhigh thinking levels differ.
technical.reproducibility: No independent matched reproduction was inspected. Google’s model card says the full safety report will follow.
technical.strongest_baseline: Google compares Hydrogen with Gemini 3.8 Flash on Terminal-Bench 4.1 and Gemini 4 Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index; Orchestrator results are compared with Carbon. Comparisons use different benchmark versions and do not establish general superiority.

brief.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen with broad availability and agentic-workflow claims
brief.why_it_matters: If its reported results generalize, a broadly available model designed for faster execution and delegation could affect agent-stack design, model routing and cost/performance choices. The launch establishes availability and price claims; it does not establish independent task performance or realized savings.

other.title: Google opens Gemini 4 Carbon to broader developer, enterprise and research access
other.summary: On Nov. 10 Google announced broader access to Gemini 4 Carbon after an earlier limited cyber-defender release. The new post describes paid developer and enterprise access, a staged Google AI Ultra subscriber rollout and expanded research access, while reporting coding, cyber and scientific results. Carbon’s model card and safety report are now inspected: Google says its Frontier Safety Framework found no material capability change over Argon and carried forward Argon’s prior threshold determinations, while also noting higher cyber benchmark scores and strengthened cyber misuse safeguards. These are provider-authored assessments, not independent reproductions. This review did not test API access or reproduce benchmarks.
